statement: List P is the arithmetic sequence $3, 10, 17, 24, \ldots$ with $100$ terms. List Q is the arithmetic sequence $5, 16, 27, 38, \ldots$ with $100$ terms. How many numbers appear in both lists?

choices.misconception: I found the common numbers $38, 115, \ldots, 654$ and divided the gap $654 - 38$ by $77$ to get $8$, forgetting to count the first one.
I used List Q's last term, $1094$, as the cutoff and divided $1094 - 38$ by $77$ to get $13$. But a common number must also be in List P, which stops at $696$, and I also forgot to count $38$ itself.
I counted the common numbers $38, 115, \ldots$ all the way up to List Q's last term, $1094$, forgetting that List P stops at $696$.
I thought the common numbers repeat every $7 + 11 = 18$, so I counted $38, 56, 74, \ldots$ up to $696$. The common numbers repeat every $7 \times 11 = 77$.

hints: Find the smallest number in both lists by checking the first few terms of List Q against List P.
A number is in List P when it is $3$ more than a multiple of $7$. Check $5, 16, 27, 38$. After the first common number, they repeat every $7 \times 11 = 77$.
The common numbers are $38, 115, 192, \ldots$, and they can be no bigger than $696$, the last term of List P.

solutions.reliable: List P is the numbers $7k + 3$ for $k = 0, 1, \ldots, 99$, ending at $696$. List Q is the numbers $11j + 5$ for $j = 0, 1, \ldots, 99$, ending at $1094$. Checking Q's terms $5, 16, 27, 38$ against P, we find $38 = 7 \cdot 5 + 3$, so $38$ is the first common number. Since $7$ and $11$ share no factor, adding $77$ keeps a number in both patterns, and nothing smaller does, so the common numbers are $38, 115, 192, 269, 346, 423, 500, 577, 654$. The next one, $731$, is past $696$, the end of List P. So $9$ numbers appear in both lists.
